title: Cloud host provider protocol
description: The cloud_hosts extension point's calls (version 1; docs/design/machine-cloud-ops.md): the manager asks a provider's program which instances its accounts hold (cloud.instances), how one is now (cloud.instance), to act on one (cloud.action: power, the address read back, a snapshot, a console link or a custom action the manifest declares; only after the gate of the action's safety level passed) and which snapshots it has (cloud.snapshots, optional). An action is a request: what follows is read from the instance's state, there are no jobs. Every params object carries contribution (the cloud_hosts item's id) and locale (the caller's language: the words the program writes, message and state_detail, are in it). The provider's credentials are its own secrets: no call carries one, and no answer may. The apps read the manager's routes' answers (CloudProviders, CloudHosts, CloudMachine, CloudBindings, CloudActionOutcome, CloudSnapshots, CloudAudit, CloudError).

CloudAccountID.description: A provider's own name for a set of credentials, a project or a panel login: opaque to the hub, never a secret.

CloudInstanceID.description: An instance's id at its vendor: opaque to the hub, kept as given.

CloudSnapshotID.description: A snapshot's id at its vendor.

CloudRequestID.description: One request to act, the same for its retries.

CloudMachineID.description: A computer's id at the hub.

CloudCustomActionID.description: A custom action's id, as the manifest declares it (manifest.schema.json ID).

CloudMessage.description: One line for people, in the reader's language: why something failed or was refused.

CloudErrorCode.description: error.code a provider answers besides the base ErrorCode: not_found (no such instance or account, or the credentials cannot see it), not_signed_in (credentials are missing, expired or refused: the user sets them in the extension's settings), unsupported (this instance has no such action), invalid_state (the action does not apply to the state the instance is in, such as start on a running one), rate_limited (the vendor's API asks to slow down), capacity (the vendor has no capacity or quota for it now, such as a spot instance that cannot be placed), refused (the vendor said no: say why in message), failed (anything else, say why in message). The manager shows the message on one line, clipped.

CloudInstanceState.description: An instance's state in the words every vendor's are mapped to: running; stopped (off, and can be started); starting; stopping; rebooting; preempted (a spot instance the vendor took back: off, and start may bring it back); terminated (gone or being deleted: nothing acts on it); unknown (the provider cannot say).

CloudActionKind.description: What can be asked of an instance. Power: start, stop (a graceful shutdown), reboot (a graceful restart), hard_reset (reset without shutting the system down), force_stop (power off without shutting it down). Operations: sync_ip (read its addresses back from the vendor now), snapshot_list (its snapshots, asked with cloud.snapshots, never cloud.action), snapshot_create, console (a link to its page or console at the vendor), custom (one of the manifest's custom_actions, named by its id). The safety level of each is the hub's (manifest.schema.json CloudSafety): sync_ip, snapshot_list and console read; start, stop, reboot and snapshot_create confirm; hard_reset and force_stop destructive; a custom action's is the manifest's.

CloudActionStatus.description: cloud.action's answer: done (it has taken effect: instance, snapshot or url say what is there now), accepted (the vendor took the request and the instance is on its way: read its state to follow), refused (nothing happened; message says why).

CloudSnapshotState.description: A snapshot: creating, ready, failed or deleting.

CloudInstanceRef.description: One instance of a provider: the account that holds it (the provider's own name for a set of credentials, a project or a panel login, never a secret) and its id at the vendor. Both are opaque to the hub and kept as given.

CloudSpec.description: An instance's size. size is the vendor's name for it (its instance type, machine type or shape); cpu its virtual CPUs (a burstable share may be a fraction); memory_mb and disk_gb what it has.

CloudLifecycle.description: What ends or interrupts an instance. spot: the vendor may take it back at any time (spot, preemptible). expires_at: when what was paid for ends. renews_at: when it is charged or renewed next. keepalive_at: by when the account has to show activity to keep it (a free tier's idle rule). auto_renew: it renews by itself.

CloudInstance.description: One instance as its provider reads it. account and id name it (CloudInstanceRef); display_name is what people call it. public_ips and private_ips are plain IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, the one to reach it by first. console_url is an https address of its page at the vendor, without credentials. actions are what can be asked of this instance now (never custom; snapshot_list means cloud.snapshots answers), custom_actions the manifest's custom actions that apply to it. observed_at is when the provider read it from the vendor. state_detail says more about the state in the caller's language, one line.

CloudInstancesParams.description: cloud.instances: every instance of every account the provider is set up with. refresh asks it not to answer from its own cache.

CloudInstanceList.description: The provider's instances, at most 500. partial when the list may be incomplete (an account could not be read: detail says which, in the caller's language). instances may be left out when there are none.

CloudInstanceParams.description: cloud.instance: how one instance is now. refresh asks the vendor rather than the provider's cache. Answered with the CloudInstance of that account and id, or not_found.

CloudActionParams.description: cloud.action: act on one instance. action is never snapshot_list; custom carries the manifest's custom action id in custom. name is a new snapshot's name (snapshot_create). The gate of the action's safety level has passed before the program hears of it. request_id is the same for a retry of the same request: a program that already did it answers what it answered.

CloudActionResult.description: cloud.action's answer (CloudActionStatus). instance is the instance after the request when the program knows it (sync_ip always answers it); snapshot the one snapshot_create made; url what console opens: an https address, which may be signed and short-lived (expires_at). message is one line for people in the caller's language: why it was refused, or what a custom action found.

CloudSnapshotsParams.description: cloud.snapshots: one instance's snapshots, newest first. Asked only of an instance whose actions name snapshot_list.

CloudSnapshotList.description: An instance's snapshots, at most 200. snapshots may be left out when there are none; the manager's answer to the apps always has it.

CloudProvider.description: One enabled cloud_hosts contribution, as the manager lists it for the apps.

CloudProviders.description: GET /api/v1/extensions/-/cloud: the enabled providers. No program is asked.

CloudHostAction.description: One thing the apps can ask of a host, with the gate the hub holds it to (safety). id, title and confirm_text are a custom action's, from the manifest.

CloudHost.description: One instance as the manager gives it to the apps: its provider (extension, provider, provider_name, vendor), the instance as the program answered it and the hub re-checked it, the actions it takes with their safety levels, and machine_id when a computer is bound to it.

CloudProviderProblem.description: A provider whose instances could not be listed: code is a CloudError code, error says why in the reader's language.

CloudHosts.description: GET /api/v1/extensions/-/cloud/instances: every enabled provider's instances together, the bound ones naming their computer. A provider that failed is in problems and the others' instances are still listed; partial when a provider said its own list may be incomplete.

CloudBinding.description: A computer bound to an instance: machine_id ↔ (extension, provider, account, instance). The rest is what the hub last read of it, kept so the computers' list draws a badge without asking a program: provider_name, vendor, display_name, state and public_ip as of seen_at.

CloudBindings.description: GET /api/v1/extensions/-/cloud/bindings: every binding, by machine id. No program is asked.

CloudBindRequest.description: PUT /api/v1/machines/{mid}/cloud: bind the computer to this instance (replacing its binding). The instance must be one the provider answers now, and bound to no other computer.

CloudRecoveryPhase.description: Where a start-and-reconnect is: starting (waiting for the instance to run), reconnecting (it runs: the computer's node is being connected again), done (the computer is connected), failed (error says why; the instance may still be running).

CloudRecovery.description: A start-and-reconnect the manager is running or last ran for a computer. It lives in the manager's memory: after its restart there is none, and the instance's state and the computer's own Reconnect say the rest. ip_changed: the instance came back with another public address than the binding last had.

CloudMachine.description: GET /api/v1/machines/{mid}/cloud: the computer's binding and, when the provider answered, its host now. bound false: no binding, nothing else. problem: the provider could not be asked or failed (the binding still stands), with a CloudError code. recovery: a start-and-reconnect in progress or just ended.

CloudActionRequest.description: POST /api/v1/machines/{mid}/cloud/actions, an app's request on the instance the computer is bound to. id names a custom action. confirm: a person agreed to exactly this action (needed for safety confirm and destructive, else confirmation_required). acknowledge: the instance's id typed or shown back (needed for destructive, else acknowledgement_required). name: a new snapshot's name. reconnect (start only): once the instance runs, connect the computer's node again (CloudRecovery).

CloudActionOutcome.description: The actions route's answer: status done or accepted (a refusal is a CloudError), the host after it when the program said, the snapshot it made, the url to open (console), the provider's one line (message) and the start-and-reconnect it began (recovery).

CloudSnapshots.description: GET /api/v1/machines/{mid}/cloud/snapshots: the bound instance's snapshots, newest first.

CloudAuditEntry.description: One audited change: a bind, an unbind or an action asked of an instance, with who asked (actor: a device, or the assistant for a tool call a person approved) and how it ended (outcome: done, accepted, refused, failed). Never a credential, an address or a provider's words.

CloudAudit.description: GET /api/v1/machines/{mid}/cloud/audit: what was asked of the computer's instances, newest first.

CloudError.description: A cloud route's error: error in the reader's language and a code: bad_request, read_only, not_found (no such computer, provider or instance), not_bound, already_bound (machine_id: the computer that holds the instance), confirmation_required and acknowledgement_required (safety says which gate), unsupported, invalid_state, not_signed_in, rate_limited, capacity, refused, plugin_failed (detail: the provider's own words, one line), provider_off, deadline, no_database.
